entities.summary:
Barisone I of Gallura was a medieval judge who played a significant role in the governance of Gallura from around 1170 to 1203. Born into a prominent family, he rose to prominence as the son of Constantine III and served as the Judge of Gallura, overseeing the administration of the region during a period of relative peace and stability.


The exact dates of his birth and death are unknown, but his legacy is evident in the numerous acts and documents that record his activities and decisions. These records provide valuable insights into the administrative and judicial practices of the medieval period in Gallura.


Despite the lack of detailed information about his personal life, Barisone I's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the governance of Gallura, which he helped shape through his judicial decisions and administrative practices. His legacy has endured through the centuries, with his name appearing in historical records and documents that continue to be studied by scholars today.


A lasting cultural footprint of Barisone I can be seen in the continued relevance of the judicial system he helped establish, which remains an important part of Galluran law and tradition.
